{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABZif2dw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhDJQiw", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 65, "title": "Correct V30MZ successful byte DIV flags and multiplication history", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `144eaef001109cf79d42f5b8426156fe2a6145ec`, successful unsigned byte division (`F6 /6`) in `crates/ws-core/src/cpu.rs` clears OF and preserves the other incoming arithmetic flags. `Cpu` stores no multiplication history. Independent WonderSwan CPU experiments report different behavior, so subsequent conditional branches can take incorrect paths. Commercial-title impact remains unmeasured.

Static reproduction, not executed during planning: seed overflowing byte IMUL with AL=10h, independently load FLAGS=F002 and AX=0006/BL=02, then execute `DIV BL`. Current code produces AX=0003/FLAGS=F002; the reported result is AX=0003/FLAGS=F843.

## Expected outcome

For successful unsigned byte DIV, clear AF/PF/SF, set ZF exactly when the remainder is zero and the quotient is odd, and restore CF/OF from the preceding multiplication rather than incoming FLAGS. Preserve unrelated control flags, quotient AL, remainder AH, operand sampling, continuation and existing instruction/bus accounting.

Apply this behavior to emulated Mono/Color/SwanCrystal model configurations independently of graphics mode. Keep multiplication history separate from architectural FLAGS.

## Context

The clean checkout and inspected remote main match the baseline. The open Issue/PR collection is empty; all 64 closed-work titles were checked. [Issue #47](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/issues/47) and [Issue #49](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/issues/49) explicitly deferred unsigned byte-DIV history. Existing `divide_tests.rs` even contains an assertion preserving its old behavior.

The [NEC preliminary manual, §3.1.5](https://www.renesas.com/en/document/lbr/v30mztm-hardware-preliminary) leaves several division flags unspecified and specifies cleared overflow. The console-specific [WSCPUTest report](https://github.com/FluBBaOfWard/WSCPUTest/blob/245b12c06dede4a2bb9c04c942ebca2044ba4930/README.md) instead reports multiplication-derived CF/OF for unsigned byte DIV. Its [assembly experiment](https://github.com/FluBBaOfWard/WSCPUTest/blob/245b12c06dede4a2bb9c04c942ebca2044ba4930/WSCpuTest.asm#L5149) changes incoming FLAGS independently; the calculator seeds history using byte `IMUL AL` with AL=00h or 10h before deriving expected results.

Producer reconciliation: byte IMUL is directly demonstrated. Interpret the report’s preceding multiplication as the explicit multiplication instructions `F6/F7 /4`, `F6/F7 /5`, `69` and `6B`; document that extending the demonstrated producer to these other forms is an instruction-level inference. Do not present it as separate measured evidence. Effects of implicit conversion microcode remain uncharacterized. No per-model measurement logs were independently inspected.

Correction record: replace the assumptions that unsigned byte DIV preserves unspecified flags and that every successful division clears OF. Correct the affected byte-DIV preservation assertions, including the universal OF test, while retaining valid word-DIV/IDIV and byte-IDIV requirements. Record old assumption, corrected requirement, source and rationale. Evidence-based corrections require no human approval or independent AI re-review; do not weaken acceptance to accommodate failures.

Scope includes successful byte DIV, explicit multiplication-history producers, lifecycle handling and necessary native/Wasm/browser coverage. Preserve existing fault behavior; exceptional division flags/results, conversion-history effects, single-step delivery and absolute timing remain visible separate gaps. A deterministic cleared history at synthetic CPU initialization is an emulator startup policy, not an established firmware-handoff value.

[Saved #63 validation](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/144eaef001109cf79d42f5b8426156fe2a6145ec/docs/issue-63-validation.md) reports 209 workspace tests and complete production Chromium suites passing. These are saved execution results, not planning-time reruns; existing tests alone do not establish this correction.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement the successful `F6 /6` rule through ordinary decoding. Retain multiplication history independently of live FLAGS; update it for the explicit producer forms listed above. Record direct evidence, applicability inferences and remaining uncertainty. Preserve multiplication products/flags and signed/word division behavior.
- [ ] Add independent literal AX/full-FLAGS expectations with both history values and opposing incoming flags. Include: clear history, AX=0006/BL=02/F002 → AX=0003/F042; set history with the same inputs → AX=0003/F843; clear history, AX=0007/BL=02/FFD7 → AX=0103/F702; set history with those inputs → AX=0103/FF03. Cover zero, exact/inexact division, odd/even quotients and quotient FFh. Expectations must not call production flag helpers.
- [ ] Exercise fit/overflow producers for byte/word MUL/IMUL and both immediate IMUL encodings, including sign extension and source/destination aliases. Demonstrate history surviving independent FLAGS replacement and intervening nonmultiplication instructions, replacement by a later producer, and repeated successful DIV operations. Preserve history across CPU cloning; prevent leakage across reset, restart, successful cartridge replacement and model changes. Failed loads/model changes must preserve the running state. Label initialization policy honestly.
- [ ] Cover register divisors, successful AL/AH aliases, mapped RAM/ROM/SRAM byte divisors at even/odd addresses and segment overrides. Assert sampled operands, untouched source memory/unrelated state, exact IP and subsequent Z/C/O/S/P/signed-condition branches. Preserve the existing 24-clock execution component and access charges; verify returned costs advance shared devices exactly once through the normal machine path.
- [ ] Cover emulated Mono/Color/SwanCrystal model configurations, all supported graphics modes and runtime mode transitions. Record actual pre-fix focused native-test and original native-probe failures, followed by corrected passes. Preserve existing division faults, arithmetic, prefixes, interrupts, HALT and DMA regressions; revise contradictory byte-DIV expectations with the documented correction rather than deleting coverage.
- [ ] Add an original source-included CC0 fixture using existing tooling, or extend `fixtures/divide.asm`. Native and production Chromium/Wasm checks must compare actual CPU-written AX, full FLAGS, history-discriminating branches and fresh execution counters on every model and restart. Poison stale observations and invalidate completion before execution. Preserve existing word-DIV/IDIV and byte-IDIV observations.
- [ ] Before merge, the Coordinator runs `python3 fixtures/build.py --check`, `python3 demo/build.py --check`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `git diff --check`. In `web`, run `npm run build:wasm`, `npm run build`, then complete `npm run test:browser` and `npm run test:compat` sequentially against the production preview. Preserve model gates, firmware-free startup, video/input/frame continuity, audio/PCM, GDMA/SDMA/Hyper Voice, SRAM/EEPROM/RTC retention, browser save integrity and ownership/provenance.
- [ ] Update hardware-support, source-reconciliation and fixture-provenance documentation. Record final revision/fixture identities, commands actually executed, failures, resolutions, passes and unperformed checks. The Coordinator reviews the final diff against every checkbox and resolves blocking findings before merge. Passing original probes must not be reported as commercial-game readiness.

## Optional validation

Baseline production-browser discrimination, additional browser engines and additional lawfully available software. Physical-console comparisons and human gameplay are optional evidence and were unperformed during planning. No proprietary ROM or firmware is required.

## Required post-merge verification

None.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WonderSwan-family hardware goal.
Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance criteria when primary hardware
specifications establish the correction. Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.

This autonomous campaign has no human-approval gate. Mandatory acceptance uses
automated native and production-browser tests on the emulator's supported model
and mode configurations. Physical-console measurements and human gameplay are
optional evidence and must remain explicitly unperformed unless actually available.
Do not invent device identities, real-device results or a requirement for human
confirmation. Resolve technical errors with recorded evidence and automated checks
through the existing Coordinator workflow.
